properties.name: Noor I (Ouarzazate CSP)
properties.description: 160 MW CSP parabolic trough with 3 hours of molten-salt thermal storage. First phase of the Ouarzazate complex. Demonstrated utility-scale CSP with storage in Africa.

properties.name: Noor II (Ouarzazate CSP)
properties.description: 200 MW CSP parabolic trough with 7 hours of molten-salt storage. Enables dispatchable solar after sunset — critical for peak evening demand.

properties.name: Noor III (Ouarzazate CSP Tower)
properties.description: 150 MW CSP tower with 7.5 hours of storage. Africa's first utility-scale CSP tower. The 243m tower and 7,400 heliostats are a landmark of Morocco's clean energy transition.

properties.name: Noor IV (Ouarzazate PV)
properties.description: 72 MW PV plant adjacent to the Noor CSP complex. Completes the Ouarzazate site with total installed capacity of 582 MW across four technologies.

properties.name: Noor Midelt Phase I
properties.description: World's first utility-scale hybrid CSP+PV with 5 hours of molten-salt storage (800 MW combined). Located on the Moulouya plateau at 1,500 m. Will deliver firm renewable power around the clock.

properties.name: Noor Laâyoune I
properties.description: 80 MW PV plant near Laâyoune in the southern provinces. Part of MASEN's program to electrify the Saharan regions from domestic renewable sources.

properties.name: Noor Boujdour I
properties.description: 20 MW PV plant near Boujdour. One of Morocco's early utility-scale PV projects in the southern provinces.

properties.name: Ain Beni Mathar ISCC (Solar Component)
properties.description: 20 MW parabolic trough solar field integrated into the 472 MW Ain Beni Mathar ISCC combined cycle plant — Africa's first utility-scale solar-thermal hybrid.

properties.name: Noor Atlas / Noor Argane (Tata)
properties.description: Part of MASEN's rolling pipeline of utility-scale PV projects in the Souss-Draa corridor (Noor Atlas 800 MW + Noor Argane 200 MW programme). GHI >2,400 kWh/m²/yr.

properties.name: Sebkhate Tah Solar PV
properties.description: 500 MW planned PV project near Foum Al-Oued in the southern provinces. Part of Morocco's long-term green hydrogen and electricity export strategy.

properties.name: Tarfaya Wind Farm
properties.description: Africa's largest wind farm at commissioning (301 MW, 131 turbines × 2.3 MW). Located on the Atlantic coast near Tarfaya with capacity factors exceeding 40%. Operated under a 20-year PPA with ONEE.

properties.name: Akhfennir Wind Farm (Phase 1)
properties.description: Phase 1 of the Akhfennir wind cluster on the southern Atlantic coast. Anchors the southern end of Morocco's Atlantic wind corridor with excellent trade wind resources.

properties.name: Akhfennir Wind Farm (Phase 2)
properties.description: Phase 2 expansion of the Akhfennir complex, bringing total site capacity to 200 MW. Part of Morocco's Integrated Wind Programme.

properties.name: Amogdoul Wind Farm (Cape Sim)
properties.description: Morocco's first large wind farm, commissioned 2006 near Essaouira. Exploits the Alizé trade winds along the Atlantic coast. Preceded the large-scale Integrated Wind Programme.

properties.name: Tangier I Wind Farm (Dhar Saadane)
properties.description: 140 MW wind farm in the Tangier peninsula, commissioned 2007. One of Morocco's earliest utility-scale wind projects, benefiting from strong Strait of Gibraltar wind acceleration.

properties.name: Khalladi Wind Farm
properties.description: 120 MW IPP wind farm near Tangier, developed by Nareva. Sells under a long-term PPA.

properties.name: Haouma Wind Farm
properties.description: 50.6 MW wind farm near Ksar es-Seghir in the Strait of Gibraltar corridor, commissioned 2014 by Nareva.

properties.name: Taza Wind Farm
properties.description: 150 MW in the Rif mountain foothills near Taza. First major wind farm in Morocco's interior, demonstrating viable resources beyond the Atlantic coast.

properties.name: Midelt Wind Farm
properties.description: 210 MW wind farm on the Moulouya plateau near Midelt, co-located in the same region as the Noor Midelt solar project. Part of Morocco's integrated renewable energy zone strategy.

properties.name: Aftissat Wind Farm
properties.description: 201 MW wind farm near Boujdour in the southern provinces, commissioned 2018. Demonstrates the exceptional wind resources of the Saharan Atlantic coast, with some of the highest capacity factors in Africa.

properties.name: Foum el Oued Wind Farm
properties.description: 50.1 MW wind farm near Laayoune commissioned 2013. Part of the first tranche of Morocco's Integrated Wind Programme in the southern provinces.

properties.name: Boujdour Wind Farm
properties.description: 100 MW near Boujdour. Precursor to larger planned developments in the Saharan Atlantic corridor.

properties.name: Tanger 2 Wind Farm
properties.description: 150 MW planned wind farm in northern Morocco, part of MASEN's Integrated Wind Programme Phase 2 developed by Enel/Nareva consortium.

properties.name: Jbel Lahdid Wind Farm (Essaouira)
properties.description: 200 MW planned wind farm south of Essaouira, part of MASEN's Integrated Wind Programme Phase 2.

properties.name: Tiskrad Wind Farm (Laayoune)
properties.description: 300 MW planned wind farm near Laayoune, part of Morocco's large-scale renewable buildout in the southern provinces targeting green hydrogen export potential.

properties.name: Jorf Lasfar Thermal Complex
properties.description: Morocco's single largest power station (2,056 MW, Units 1–6). Backbone of national baseload. Shares Jorf Lasfar industrial port with OCP phosphate complex. Primary candidate for phased coal retirement under Morocco's NDC.

properties.name: Safi Coal Power Plant
properties.description: 1,386 MW coal IPP near Safi, developed by Nareva/EDF. Morocco's newest and largest coal plant. Commissioned 2017 under a 25-year PPA with ONEE.

properties.name: Nador West Med Coal Plant
properties.description: 1,320 MW coal plant under construction at Nador West Med industrial port. Controversial given Morocco's RE targets. When complete will add significant baseload capacity in the northeastern grid.

properties.name: Ain Beni Mathar ISCC
properties.description: Africa's first ISCC plant: 20 MW parabolic trough + 452 MW gas CCGT. Located in the Oriental region. The solar component displaces ~12,000 t CO₂/yr.

properties.name: Tahaddart CCGT
properties.description: Morocco's first IPP under a BOT contract (384 MW). Receives Algerian gas via the Maghreb–Europe Pipeline. Serves as mid-merit capacity for the northern grid and Spain interconnect.

properties.name: Mohammedia Thermal Plant
properties.description: 600 MW aging HFO plant near Mohammedia. Increasingly operated as strategic reserve given high marginal costs vs renewables. Candidate for decommissioning or flexibility conversion.

properties.name: Jerada Coal Plant
properties.description: 515 MW coal plant at Jerada in the Oriental region. Located near Morocco's historic coal mining basin. Subject to social pressure from local communities following a 2017–2018 protest movement.

properties.name: Kenitra Thermal Plant
properties.description: 615 MW mixed coal/gas plant at Kenitra (300 MW coal + 315 MW gas units). Serves the Rabat–Kenitra industrial corridor.

properties.name: Afourer Pumped Storage (STEP)
properties.description: 465 MW pumped storage facility (STEP Afourer) in the High Atlas, operational since 2004. Morocco's largest grid flexibility asset — stores surplus overnight generation and dispatches during morning/evening peaks.

properties.name: Abdelmoumen Pumped Storage (STEP)
properties.description: 350 MW STEP in the Souss-Massa region. Morocco's next major pumped storage project, critical for absorbing variable RE as the country targets 52% renewable by 2030.

properties.name: Bin el Ouidane Dam
properties.description: 135 MW on the Oued El Abid in the High Atlas. One of Morocco's oldest hydroelectric facilities; output highly variable with precipitation.

properties.name: Al Wahda Dam
properties.description: 240 MW on the Oued Ouerrha in the Rif. Africa's second-largest dam by storage volume. Provides both power and irrigation for the Gharb plain.

properties.name: Allal al Fassi Dam
properties.description: 240 MW reservoir plant on the Oued Ouerrha, commissioned 1994.

properties.name: Al Massira Dam
properties.description: 128 MW on the Oued Oum er-Rbia near Settat. Major water supply reservoir for the Doukkala-Abda region.

properties.name: Hassan II Dam (STEP)
properties.description: 180 MW STEP in the Middle Atlas. Morocco's first pumped storage facility, providing peaking capacity and frequency regulation.

properties.name: Idriss I Dam
properties.description: 40 MW on the Oued Inaouène. Part of Morocco's historic hydroelectric network in the Middle Atlas.

properties.name: Hassan I Dam
properties.description: 67 MW on the Oued El Abid near Demnate in the High Atlas.
